Physics (MS, PhD)
Program Overview
The Department of Physics, Applied Physics and Astronomy offers graduate programs leading to Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) and Master of Science (MS) degrees. Our mission is to prepare students for successful careers in academia, national laboratories, and industry through rigorous coursework and immersive research. Students have exciting opportunities to conduct fundamental and applied research alongside internationally recognized faculty at the forefront of condensed matter physics, materials physics, ultrafast optics, and biophysics, as well as their intersection with clean energy programs. In addition to cutting-edge physics research labs, on-campus interdisciplinary facilities include the analytical and diagnostics laboratory (ADL), a clean room for device fabrication and high-performance computing.
PhD candidates are funded through teaching assistantships, research assistantships, and fellowships, which include a stipend, tuition and health insurance. MS candidates are self-funded.
We welcome applications from students who have successfully completed an undergraduate degree in physics or closely related fields. For full consideration, applications must be submitted by Jan. 15.
Application Materials
International Student Requirements
Note: GRE is optional. The minimum required TOEFL score is 80
We are able to waive the application fee for a limited number of qualified PhD candidates who submit a request by Jan. 1. To be considered for the waiver, you should start your application and ask your references to provide their recommendation letters. Once you upload all application documents, submit the Physics Fee Waiver Requestform. You will receive an email with a decision on your request one week before the Jan. 15 application deadline. Note that you should not submit your application package until the application fee is either paid or waived.

opportunities at Binghamton. We encourage prospective students to review available program-specific scholarships and awards,
